title: Scope of a run: rule filters and --exclude-tests write only what they see
description: An entry is in the scope of a run when its package is scanned, its rule is selected and its file is analyzed. A run filtered to some rules or without the tests treats the other entries as unknown, not stale: --create-baseline replaces only the entries in scope, --prune-baseline removes only stale entries in scope, and the stale warning counts only entries in scope. main.bal has 1 ballerina:13 and 2 ballerina:1, tests/main_test.bal 1 ballerina:1. Needs scan 0.15.0+.
upstream: BEP 1498: Finding fingerprints and baseline adoption (ballerina-spec/beps/tool-scan/1498_scan_baseline.md)

steps.name: --prune-baseline --exclude-rules=ballerina:13
steps.note: The ballerina:13 entry is out of scope, so it is not removed: "The baseline has no entries to remove", 4 entries kept.

steps.name: --exclude-tests
steps.note: The test entry is out of scope: 0 new issue(s), 2 in baseline, and only 1 stale entry (the secret).

steps.name: --create-baseline --include-rules=ballerina:13
steps.note: Replaces only the ballerina:13 entries (now none) and keeps the 3 ballerina:1 entries: "Saved 3 entries".

steps.name: Scan
steps.note: 0 new issue(s), 3 in baseline, no warning.

steps.name: --create-baseline --exclude-tests
steps.note: The test entry is kept, though the tests were not scanned: "The baseline already holds these 3 entries".
